findings.issue: The tech-spec asserts a fail-safe invariant: 'legacy old-type document that survived the manual wipe does not crash the engine on startup (tolerant-read)'. This invariant is NOT implemented. There is no custom MongoCustomConversions / @ReadingConverter for unknown StepType (or BlockType) enum values, and application.properties has no read-unknown-enum setting. A surviving funnel_executions/funnels document with stepType='MENU' (or any removed value) will fail Spring Data enum deserialization during sweep()'s mongoTemplate.find(...) — which is OUTSIDE the per-execution try/catch (that guard only wraps runExecution per row). The ConversionFailedException would abort the ENTIRE sweep tick, stalling the whole engine, not just one execution. Note: the per-execution try/catch DOES protect against a deserialized-but-malformed step (e.g. a MESSAGE step with null blocks NPEs inside one runExecution and is caught), so the gap is specifically the load-time enum conversion of an UNKNOWN value.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) implement the claimed tolerant-read (a read converter that maps unknown StepType/BlockType to a benign skip/terminal-fail sentinel), or (b) explicitly downgrade the spec/risk entry to 'accepted residual risk, mitigated operationally by the Decision-4 manual wipe (zero production data)'. Task 12 (pre-deploy QA) / Task 13 (deploy + wipe) should verify the wipe is total before relying on this. Do not leave the spec asserting an invariant the code does not provide.

findings.issue: StepExecutor.message() dereferences step.getBlocks() (blocks.size(), blocks.get(i)) with no null guard. A MESSAGE step whose snapshot has null blocks throws NPE on every sweep tick. validateMessage rejects null/empty blocks at save time, so this is unreachable on the normal path — but a directly-seeded/legacy snapshot (the same population that MAJ-1 covers) would NPE forever: the execution never terminates (the engine's per-execution try/catch catches the NPE but the row stays running/in_progress and is re-claimed next tick -> infinite log spam, stuck execution). Validation is at the API boundary; the executor (engine-internal, consumes persisted snapshots) does not defend its own precondition.
findings.recommendation: Add a defensive guard at the top of message(): if (blocks == null || blocks.isEmpty()) return StepResult.fail("empty_message_blocks") (terminal, so the stuck execution self-resolves instead of looping). Cheap, removes the infinite-retry footgun, and makes the executor robust to a malformed snapshot independent of save-time validation.

findings.file: backend/src/main/java/com/botfunnel/funnel/FunnelService.java:411,424 (previewStep/renderBlocks comments) ; backend dto PreviewStepRequest.java:7 / PreviewStepResponse.java:5 reference 'Decision 8' correctly ; frontend stores/funnels.ts:215 + frontend types/funnel.ts (preview comments) reference 'Decision 9'
findings.issue: Inconsistent Decision numbering for the preview feature. The tech-spec has exactly 8 Decisions; preview = Decision 8. Backend DTOs correctly say 'Decision 8', but FunnelService.previewStep/renderBlocks comments say 'Decision 9 / Decision 8' and frontend stores/funnels.ts:215 and several types/funnel.ts comments say 'Decision 9'. There is no Decision 9. (The album-typer correction's handoff note already flagged 'Decision 9 -> Decision 8' for types but it was not fully applied; store + FunnelService still drift.)
findings.recommendation: Normalize all preview references to 'Decision 8' across FunnelService.java, stores/funnels.ts, and remaining types/funnel.ts comments. Pure comment fix; no behavior change.

findings.issue: Dangling Javadoc reference: '{@link StepType#MENU}'. StepType.MENU was removed (Decision 4), so this @link no longer resolves. Compilation is unaffected (build.gradle has no -Xdoclint/-Werror for javadoc), but the symbol reference is broken and the comment text ('button on a MENU step') is stale — the button now lives on the MESSAGE composer's last non-album block (Decision 2).
findings.recommendation: Replace '{@link StepType#MENU}' with '{@link StepType#MESSAGE}' and update the prose to 'last non-album block of a MESSAGE composer step (Decision 2)'.

findings.file: frontend/components/funnels/FunnelMessagePreview.vue:69-72,275,280 (mediaLoadFailed keyed by block index for ALBUM)
findings.issue: For an ALBUM block, every item's calls onMediaError(index) with the BLOCK index, so a single broken album image flips the whole album block to the placeholder (all items hidden), not just the failing item. Per-item granularity is lost. Functional-not-broken, pure UX; already noted by the Task-8 self-review as accept-as-designed but re-confirmed here independently.
findings.recommendation: Optional: key album failures by composite (blockIndex, itemIndex) so one bad item degrades only that cell. Low priority — preview-only, no correctness/security impact.

findings.file: frontend/e2e/funnels.spec.ts (carried over from Wave 4 gate report)
findings.issue: e2e/funnels.spec.ts still references the removed model (helper addSendMessage on default SEND_MESSAGE, step-text-input, selectOption('MENU'), step-menu-* selectors). It is excluded from the vitest gate (include: tests/**) and runs only under pnpm test:e2e (live stack), so it compiles (selectors are string literals, no removed TS types) and did not break CI — but it is dead/stale relative to the composer UI and would fail if ever run. Out of the strict source scope of this task but it is part of the feature's removal surface.

findings.file: backend PreviewStepRequest.stepType (String) / PreviewStepResponse.RenderedBlock.type (String) vs frontend PreviewStepRequest.stepType (StepType) / RenderedBlock.type (BlockType)
findings.issue: Frontend mirrors are STRICTER (typed enum) than the backend (raw String). This is intentional and safe (backend tolerates unknown preview block types by design — preview is non-validating; frontend only ever sends valid enum values). No action needed; noting the asymmetry for completeness.

MediaItem.type reuses the BlockType enum but only IMAGE|VIDEO|AUDIO|FILE are valid (TEXT/ALBUM are nonsense for an item). The constraint is enforced only at validation (validateAlbum) and defensively at send (albumElementType throws on TEXT/ALBUM). A dedicated MediaKind enum would make illegal states unrepresentable, but reusing BlockType avoids a parallel enum + DTO and is consistent with the codebase's flat-model philosophy. Acceptable trade-off; documented in both records' Javadoc.
findings.recommendation: None (acceptable as-is). If a future phase adds more block types, revisit.

findings.issue: Per-node at-most-once (Decision 3) is correctly preserved: all N block sends run under ONE engine claim inside one try/catch; a mid-block TelegramSendException maps via fromTerminalReason (BLOCKED/CHAT_NOT_FOUND -> cancel, else fail), blocks 1..K-1 are lost-forward with no re-send. Catch arms (TelegramSendException / BotTokenInvalidException / AppException) match the former flat branches exactly. Verified consistent with Decision 3.

findings.dimension: Security (8) — cross-check only; deep audit is Task 10
findings.file: FunnelService.requireMediaSource/requireUrl/looksLikeUrl ; StepExecutor.sendBlock ; FunnelMessagePreview.vue (no v-html, http(s) scheme guard) ; renderBlocks (parseMode escaping, no dereference)
findings.issue: No gross security violations observed in scope: media URLs are never dereferenced server-side (anti-SSRF, Decision 6); strict http(s) scheme validation with leading-whitespace + empty-host rejection; backend-side parseMode escaping in preview; frontend renders text via {{ }} only (no v-html / innerHTML anywhere) and gates clickable media on http(s). Callback wire contract {executionId}:{buttonIndex} unchanged with strict parse + IDOR/owner/project checks + CAS-gated event recording. Depth of OWASP review deferred to Task 10 per task scope.
findings.recommendation: Defer detailed security findings to Task 10.

findings.issue: Snapshot isolation is correctly threaded: copyOf takes a defensive shallow copy of blocks (new ArrayList<>) — valid because ContentBlock and MediaItem are immutable records (so element sharing is safe), null stays null. deepCopySteps maps element-wise via copyOf. Verified coherent with Decision 1/3.

escalation: MAJ-1 and MAJ-2 are robustness/spec-fidelity gaps, not happy-path defects. Recommend addressing before Pre-deploy QA (Task 12): MAJ-2 is a small defensive guard; MAJ-1 needs a decision (implement tolerant-read vs. downgrade the spec invariant to accepted-residual-risk gated on a verified total wipe in Task 13). MIN-1/MIN-2 are comment-only fixes. MIN-3/MIN-4 are optional/owned-elsewhere.
